text:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: multiple serving pods in us-west-2 reporting OOMKilled + CUDA OOMs; autoscaler triggered resizes. Suspected: paged-attention allocator + KV cache growth. Alert: https://ops.redwood.example/alerts/INC-1789998888

sara_oncall: picking this up — which clusters/roles are affected? any customer impact yet?

mike_runtime: seeing it in prod-usw2 (model-serving pool) and a smaller signal in preprod-usw2. Symptoms: host RSS creeping over hours, then pod gets OOMKilled with CUDA OOM in container logs. One node (usw2-n-17) flapped.

jess_sre: kube events show repeated OOMKill -> CrashLoopBackOff then kubelet evict. dmesg on node shows "Out of memory: Killed process <pid> (serving-runtime)" followed by GPU driver complaining about context after restart.

tom_support: Customer ops — two external customers reported increased 503s and elevated latency in last 90m. Ticket ids: C-21982, C-21984. Notified account teams.

nora_eng: quick triage: heap (host-side) growth correlates with kv_cache slab usage; paged-attn allocator appears to not release pages on eviction boundary when sequence lengths are high. Likely a regression in recent allocator compaction logic (rollout 176.x).

lucy_custops: customers seeing intermittent failures during long conversations (lots of prefixing). They describe sessions that grow token count then error.

mike_runtime: attaching short log excerpt from one pod:
```
2026-02-28T02:10:12Z serving-runtime[pid=4321]: kv_cache: insert page id=0x7f9a size=2.1MiB total_pages=24192
2026-02-28T02:10:15Z serving-runtime[pid=4321]: allocator: paged-attn allocate seq=8192 pages=48
2026-02-28T02:14:03Z serving-runtime[pid=4321]: CUDA error: out of memory while allocating 1.2GiB
2026-02-28T02:14:05Z kernel: Killed process 4321 (serving-runtime) total-vm:20480000kB
```

sara_oncall: any fast mitigations we can apply while eng digs into root cause?

nora_eng: short list: 1) force KV compaction on affected pods 2) lower KVCACHE_MAX_PAGES env to throttle growth 3) enable fallback to smaller model variant for heavy sessions 4) cordon + drain the worst nodes, scale up pool temporarily.

mike_runtime: I can trigger compaction and lower env on a canary. Command to force compaction (safe but CPU-heavy):
```bash
kubectl exec -n prod svc/serving-runtime-canary -- /usr/local/bin/kv-compact --max-pass=3 --force
```
Also to flip eviction interval: `kubectl set env daemonset/serving-runtime KVCACHE_EVICT_INTERVAL=30s -n prod`

jess_sre: I'll cordon/drain usw2-n-17 and move traffic off it. Taking node out of service now.

jess_sre: node cordoned and drained (usw2-n-17). pods rescheduled.

mike_runtime: applied manual compaction on canary, then rolled the env change to the rest of the daemonset in staging, monitoring memory graphs.

(10m pass)
mike_runtime: metrics update: canary host RSS growth plateaued after compaction and eviction interval change. GPU mem no longer trending up. Rolling the env to prod in 3 batches.

tom_support: customers C-21982 and C-21984 notified: "We applied emergency mitigations; you may see transient restarts. We're monitoring and will follow up with RCA."

sara_oncall: rolling update underway. If this stabilizes, we'll keep mitigation config for 24-48h and then revert into an RC for proper fix. Assigning owner for RCA.

nora_eng: assigned to me for root cause & patch. Initial plan: reproduce with heavy long-token workloads, run allocator debug build, check compaction edgecases where page refcounts are held by in-flight KV pointers. Hypothesis: a race where eviction marks page free but paged-attn still references a stale page id during async remote call.

sara_oncall: escalation/next steps documented in incident ticket INC-1789998888. Please add logs and gcore if we hit a repro.

mike_runtime: note: permanent workaround backlog: improve compaction handshake, add metrics for page refcounts, and add automated emergency fallback to smaller model when host RSS above threshold.

jess_sre: ops checklist: 1) cordon node(s) if flapping 2) run compaction 3) adjust KVCACHE env 4) scale up pool if required 5) customer comms.

(incident status)
sara_oncall: status -> mitigated (rolling config applied, compaction complete on affected pods). Monitoring for 2h. No new OOMKills in last 12m on previous hot nodes.

lucy_custops: customers acknowledged mitigation and asked for ETA on permanent fix. I've scheduled a customer-facing summary once RCA is ready.

nora_eng: I'll open a PR with a unit/integration test for the eviction race and a small hotfix to ensure pages are pinned until async ops complete. ETA for patch + canary: 48h.

sara_oncall: thanks all. Closing active page in PagerDuty but keeping incident thread pinned until RCA posted. If anything regresses, reopen.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1789998888 status updated -> mitigated. Postmortem pending."
